intro.en: The Modified Kuppuswamy scale used to grade family socioeconomic status in the paediatric case sheet, with pedigree degrees for family history.

items.summary: Scores for the occupation of the head of the family, the first of three parts of the scale.

blocks.title: How to score
blocks.text: Take the highest scoring occupation in the household, usually the head of the family, and add its points to the education and income points before reading the class table.

head: Occupation of head of family
Score
rows: Skilled workers and shop and market sales workers

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Unemployment scores the minimum of 1, while legislators, senior officials and managers score the maximum of 10.
Skilled work outranks semi-skilled work, which outranks unskilled work.

viva.q: Which occupation scores highest on this scale?
viva.a: Legislators, senior officials and managers at 10 points.

viva.q: How do you combine the three parts of the scale?
viva.a: Add occupation, education and income points, then read the class from the total score table.

unsure: Printed occupation numbering repeats 3, 4 and 5 after row 5; rows were renumbered 1 to 10 with labels and scores unchanged.

items.summary: Scores for schooling of the head of the family, the second of three parts of the scale.

blocks.title: How to score
blocks.text: Take the schooling level reached by the head of the family and add its points to the occupation and income points before reading the class table.

head: Education of head of family
Score
rows: Intermediate or post high school diploma

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Each step of schooling adds one point, from 1 for no schooling to 7 for a profession or honours degree.
A graduate scores 6 while an intermediate pass scores 5.

viva.q: What does a graduate score for education?
viva.a: 6 points, one below a profession or honours degree at 7.

viva.q: What does a middle school certificate score?
viva.a: 3 points, midway between illiterate at 1 and high school at 4.

items.summary: Scores for total monthly family income in rupees, the third of three parts of the scale.

blocks.title: Which revision
blocks.text: Income bands follow the March 2018 revision published in the Paripex Indian Journal of Research, volume 7, issue 3.

head: Family income per month in rupees
Score

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Income carries the widest span of points, from 1 to 12.
Use total family income per month, not the income of one earner alone.

viva.q: What is the highest income score and its band?
viva.a: 12 points for 126,360 rupees and above per month.
Total monthly family income, not one earner alone.

viva.q: Why does income carry the most points?
viva.a: It spans 1 to 12, the widest range of the three parts.

unsure: Income bands were kept exactly as printed, but the second band reads 63,182 to 12,656 with the upper bound below the lower, and small gaps sit between bands; flagged for review against the 2018 revision.

title.en: Kuppuswamy scale: total score and class

items.summary: Total points from occupation, education and income mapped to five socioeconomic classes.

blocks.title: How to use it
blocks.text: Add the three component scores, find the band holding the total, and record both the class name and its roman numeral on the case sheet.

viva.q: A family totals 20 points. Which class?
viva.a: Upper middle, class II, which spans 16 to 25.

viva.q: What is the highest possible total?
viva.a: 29, from 10 for occupation, 7 for education and 12 for income.

viva.q: A family totals 8 points. Which class?
viva.a: Lower upper lower, class IV, which spans 5 to 10.

items.summary: Degrees of blood relatives by share of genes, used when drawing the family tree.

blocks.title: The three degrees
bullets: First degree: parents, children and siblings, sharing 50 percent of genes.
Second degree: uncles, aunts, nieces, nephews and grandparents, sharing 25 percent of genes.
Third degree: cousins, sharing 12.5 percent of genes.

viva.q: Who counts as a first degree relative?
viva.a: Parents, children and siblings, sharing 50 percent of genes.
Third degree relatives, sharing 12.5 percent of genes.
